question.problem:
Given the system of equations below, what is the value of $a+b?$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2b=6a+14 \\ 5b+25=0\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
We number the equations so that we can refer to them more easily:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2b=6a+14 & \,\,(1) \\ 5b+25=0. & \,\,(2)\end{aligned}
$$

We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. Using equation $(2),$ we can solve for $b$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5b+25 & =0 \\ 5b & =-25 \\ b & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $b=-5$ into equation $(1)$ and solve for $a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2(-5) & =6a+14 \\ -10 & =6a+14 \\ -10-14 & =6a \\ 6a & =-24 \\ a & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $a=-4,\,b=-5.$ So,

$$
a+b=-4+(-5)=-4-5=-9.
$$
